# Common generic defaults

Generated designs currently cluster around a few looks. Each can be right for some brief, but they appear regardless of subject, so they read as defaults rather than choices. Use one only when the brief or brand asks for it, or when you can explain why it fits this subject better than anything else.

1. **Warm cream and clay.** A cream background (around #F4F1EA), a high-contrast serif display face and a terracotta or warm clay accent (around #D97757). This accent is closely associated with one well-known AI product, so on a client's brief it reads as a giveaway.
2. **Dark with one acid accent.** A near-black background with a single bright acid green or vermilion accent.
3. **Broadsheet.** Hairline rules, zero corner radius and dense newspaper-style columns.
4. **The SaaS card kit.** Content cut into identical rounded cards, one corner radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow under each card, and gradient washes as decoration.
5. **Template chrome.** A spaced-out all-caps label above every heading; details joined with middle dots ("A · B · C"); labels written as a word, a spaced long dash and a fragment; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) used instead of black; a monospace face for small data labels; an arrow added to every link and button.

## Typographic habits to avoid by default

- Highlighting a single word or phrase in a headline with italic, bold or color.
- All-caps labels.
- Labels added above content that do not carry information.
- Numbered markers (01, 02, 03) on content that is not a sequence.

## Motion habits to avoid by default

- Fade-and-slide-up entrance on every section.
- Hover transitions on every card.

## Structure is information

Borders, numbering, dividers and labels should encode something true about the content (a sequence, a grouping, a status). If a device decorates without informing, remove it.
